AI Compliance Toolkit: EU AI Act + GDPR.

Your team already uses ChatGPT, Copilot and other AI tools. Under the EU AI Act, businesses must already make sure staff who use AI have sufficient AI literacy. This toolkit helps you get control of it in an afternoon.

EU AI Act + GDPR

What's in the kit

  • Guide — the EU and national rules at a glance, a step-by-step setup and a 6-month review routine
  • Approved AI Tools Registry — every AI tool, its EU AI Act risk tier, review status and next review date
  • GDPR checkpoints for every tool that processes personal data
  • AI Employee Policy — ready to adapt, just fill in your company details
  • Two training video scripts to record your own staff training
  • Training Log — who has been trained and when, as proof of AI literacy
  • Incident log and review & sign-off with an automatic next review date

The rules it covers

  • AI literacy (Art. 4 AI Act)

    Has applied since 2 February 2025 to every business that uses AI systems, including everyday tools like chatbots and writing assistants.

  • Risk tiers

    The AI Act sorts uses into prohibited, high-risk, limited-risk and minimal-risk. Knowing which tier each tool falls into tells you what else you have to do.

  • GDPR still applies

    As soon as personal data goes into a prompt, the GDPR applies: legal basis, transparency, processor agreements and transfers outside the EU.

Made for

  • Businesses whose staff use AI tools
  • Founders and managing directors
  • HR and operations managers
  • IT and data protection coordinators

Questions about this kit

Does the AI Act apply if we only use ChatGPT or Copilot?
Yes. As a business that uses AI systems you are a “deployer”, and the AI literacy duty in Art. 4 already applies to you. Most of the heavier obligations only apply to high-risk uses, such as AI in recruitment.
How do I prove AI literacy?
The AI Act does not prescribe a certificate. What helps is a record: which tools are approved, what the rules are, and who has been trained when. The registry, policy and training log give you exactly that.
What is the difference from the AI Workplace Policy Pack?
This toolkit is about governing the tools: register, risk tiers, GDPR checks and reviews. The Policy Pack is about the people: the policy, staff guide, acknowledgments and tool requests. Many businesses use both.
